"We appreciate everything Lane has contributed to our organization, and we wish him and his family nothing but the best." Johnson helped the Eagles win Super Bowls LII and LIX. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em quedas com ajuste após rali eleitoral
item.description: O Ibovespa encerrou a terça-feira em queda, com os investidores fazendo ajustes de posições após o forte rali da véspera, quando o índice atingiu máximas históricas em meio à euforia nos mercados locais com o resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa encerrou a terça-feira em queda, com os investidores fazendo ajustes de posições após o forte rali da véspera, quando o índice atingiu máximas históricas em meio à euforia nos mercados locais com o resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) caiu 0,52%, a 205.835,29 pontos, após marcar 204.725,23 na mínima e 209.522,60 na máxima do dia. O volume financeiro no pregão somou R$58,06 bilhões. A correção na bolsa acontece após o Ibovespa atingir na véspera o maior nível intradiário, aos 209 mil pontos, e o recorde de fechamento, a 206.911,89 pontos. Os recordes foram uma resposta ao resultado eleitoral de domingo, que mostrou Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à frente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na disputa presidencial. "O mercado hoje realiza eventuais lucros. O investidor revê os preços que ficaram esticados de determinados ativos. Então é relativamente normal termos um período de respiro em altas tão grandes", disse Willian Queiroz, sócio e advisor da Blue3 Investimentos. Ainda assim, mesmo com o recuo, o Ibovespa seguiu operando acima dos 200 mil pontos. "Com este movimento, o índice confirma a volta à tendência de alta e passa a apontar para a região de 220.000 pontos no curto prazo e 245.000 pontos no médio prazo", disse o Itaú BBA em seu relatório Diário do Grafista. Segundo os analistas do banco, para manter a tendência de alta, "o Ibovespa terá que continuar acima do suporte em 181.500 pontos". Em Nova York, as bolsas subiram com a queda do petróleo e a retração de rendimentos dos Treasuries. O S&P 500 (.SPX) subiu 0,57%. DESTAQUES PETROBRAS PN recuou 2,78% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) perdeu 1,8%, na esteira do desempenho do petróleo no exterior, que recuou pela maior parte da sessão mas fechou em leve alta, com o Brent subindo 0,26%. ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN subiu 1,96%, BRADESCO PN avançou 4,4%, SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT subiu 3,23% e BTG PACTUAL recuou 2,81%. BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) recuou 6,42%, liderando as quedas do Ibovespa. Pela manhã, o JP Morgan [USN:L1N45S0MW TEXT:"rebaixou"] a recomendação para o papel de "neutro" para "underweight". VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuou 1,44%. No setor, USIMINAS PNA recuou 1,88%, enquanto GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) teve declínio de 1,01%.

item.title: Rays know job isn't done as they face desperate Yankees in Game 3
item.description: NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Tampa Bay Rays enjoyed clinching the American League East at Yankee Stadium but also viewed the celebration as the first step.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK -- Two weeks ago, the Tampa Bay Rays enjoyed clinching the American League East at Yankee Stadium but also viewed the celebration as the first step. Now the Rays are one win away from another raucous party, and the New York Yankees are desperate to delay it. The Rays attempt to complete a sweep of the American League Division Series while the Yankees hope to clean up their mistakes and get their bats going in Game 3 on Wednesday night. Right-hander Nick Martinez will start for Tampa Bay and will be opposed by left-hander Max Fried. Tampa Bay batted .248 against left-handed pitching during the regular season. "If we don't win, we go home, and this is where you leave everything out on the field," Fried said Tuesday. "There's nothing else to save anything for." The Rays are seeking their first trip to the ALCS since 2020, when they won a five-game ALDS against the Yankees. Overall, Tampa Bay has reached the ALCS twice in its 29-year history, also advancing in 2008 when it posted its first winning record and reached the World Series. After winning 98 games and clinching their fifth AL East title in team history on Sept. 22, the Rays hold a 2-0 lead in the Division Series for the second time in their history thanks to 1-0 and 5-2 victories. "It's pretty significant," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said about winning the first two games. "We're getting ready to go to a place (where the Yankees thrive). They have a tremendous fan base that really supports them. It's going to be challenging, but, I mean, we've set ourselves up in a good way by getting on a plane here up 2-0." "It's definitely a good feeling to take the first two, but definitely not putting the gas down on these next ones," Rays outfielder Jonny DeLuca added. "Hopefully, we can get it done Wednesday." The Rays opened the series with a combined one-hitter from Drew Rasmussen and Bryan Baker, along with a home run by Jonathan Aranda off Gerrit Cole. On Monday, Tampa Bay scored three unearned runs, and Richie Palacios had a two-run single in a four-run fifth inning. After committing 96 errors during the regular season, New York was charged with at least three unearned runs in a playoff game for the second time in three seasons and the 15th time overall. Ryan McMahon booted Yandy Diaz's grounder to third, second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. made an errant throw on Junior Caminero's grounder and Austin Wells was called for catcher's interference in the first inning. Later on, rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. committed a throwing error just before Palacios singled, continuing a display that resembled Game 5 of the 2024 World Series against the Dodgers. New York is trying to overcome a 2-0 deficit in the Division Series for the third time after also doing so in 2017 against Cleveland and 2001 against the A's. Ben Rice homered twice Monday, but the offense-starved Yankees are 5-for-58 with 19 strikeouts after hitting .382 against the Red Sox. The Yankees used the same lineup in the first two games, using eight left-handed hitters, and it is possible they make some changes. Manager Aaron Boone said during Tuesday's off-day availability he was considering mixing up a lineup that had two at-bats with runners in scoring position in the opening two games. "Obviously we're completely up against it now," Boone said Tuesday afternoon. "So we got to bring it tomorrow night. But it's that level of focus with some calm to the whole situation, too, because you don't want to get in a situation where you're pressing out there, trying to do more than you're capable of. It's about doing your job right now." If the Yankees win, Game 4 will be Thursday night. --Larry Fleisher, Field Level Media

item.title: Aneel adia decisão sobre caducidade da Enel São Paulo por pedido da vista
item.description: A diretoria da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) adiou uma decisão sobre a recomendação de caducidade do contrato da distribuidora Enel São Paulo, em processo que começou a ser votado nesta terça-feira, mas foi paralisado por pedido de vista do diretor Gentil Nogueira.
item.dc:creator: Leticia Augusto
item.content:encoded: A diretoria da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) adiou uma decisão sobre a recomendação de caducidade do contrato da distribuidora Enel São Paulo, em processo que começou a ser votado nesta terça-feira, mas foi paralisado por pedido de vista do diretor Gentil Nogueira. A diretora relatora do caso, Agnes da Costa, apresentou mais cedo na reunião desta terça-feira um extenso voto favorável à recomendação de caducidade da concessão da distribuidora paulista ao Ministério de Minas e Energia. O posicionamento foi acompanhado pela diretora Ludimila Lima, mas o processo de votação foi interrompedido pelo pedido de vista apresentado por Nogueira. Ele disse querer aprofundar sua análise sobre o voto da relatora, citando por exemplo recentes apontamentos feitos pelo [USN:L1N45F0VY TEXT:"Tribunal de Contas da União"] sobre a necessidade de estudos de alternativas à caducidade. Em seu voto, Costa rejeitou argumentos que já haviam sido apresentados anteriormente pela Enel. Ela defendeu que a recomendação de caducidade é o último recurso que a Aneel dispõe para tratar do caso, depois que todos os instrumentos mobilizados nos últimos anos, como planos de resultados firmados consensualmente com a distribuidora e a aplicação de multas milionárias, não foram suficientes para induzir a melhora efetiva na prestação dos serviços. A diretora ressaltou que a recomendação de caducidade, conforme sua proposta, resulta de um conjunto "robusto e convergente" de elementos técnicos, jurídicos e probatórios reunidos em um longo processo, que contou com consultas à área técnica da agência e à Procuradoria Federal, além de espaço para ampla defesa da distribuidora. Entre os argumentos rejeitados, Costa apontou, por exemplo, que a Enel vem se utilizando desde 2023 da tese de que tempestades severas "imprevisíveis" afetaram suas operações em São Paulo, ao danificar a rede elétrica devido à queda de árvores, cabos e postes. Segundo a relatora, ao mobilizar esse mesmo argumento por anos, a empresa buscou "esquivar-se de responsabilidades na ocorrência de eventos climáticos de maior magnitude, ao invés de enfrentá-los, mesmo sabendo que ocorrem com certa frequência". DEFESA DA ENEL Durante a reunião da Aneel nesta terça-feira, um porta-voz da Enel apresentou novamente a defesa da empresa no caso. Entre os pontos destacados, estão um aumento de 70% dos investimentos na concessão paulista, a melhora dos tempos de atendimentos emergenciais e a falta de análise e comprovação de que a caducidade é a alternativa mais vantajosa para os consumidores e para a prestação dos serviços. Também apresentaram manifestações em defesa da Enel sindicatos de trabalhadores do setor, como o dos eletricitários, e 22 prefeitos dos 24 municípios da região metropolitana de São Paulo atendidos pela distribuidora. A capital paulista, governada pelo prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB), que vinha defendendo a saída da empresa da concessão, não foi citada nesse grupo de defesa. Os serviços de distribuição de energia da Enel no Brasil têm estado sob forte escrutínio público desde o fim de 2023, quando concessionárias da empresa levaram dias para restabelecer a energia aos consumidores após eventos climáticos extremos. Situações similares nos anos seguintes agravaram o problema da companhia italiana no Brasil. Com uma base de mais de 8 milhões de consumidores, a distribuidora paulista é a maior do portfólio da Enel no Brasil, onde opera ainda no Ceará e Rio de Janeiro. As três empresas da Enel têm concessões vencendo até meados de 2028, e as potenciais renovações desses contratos por mais 30 anos ainda estão pendentes.

item.title: Ex-chefe do serviço secreto alemão é preso por tentativa de traição e obtenção de segredos de Estado
item.description: O ex-chefe do serviço secreto alemão August Hanning foi detido nesta terça-feira sob suspeita de tentativa de traição, em um caso que figura entre os maiores escândalos de inteligência da Alemanha desde a Guerra Fria.
item.dc:creator: Friederike Heine
item.content:encoded: O ex-chefe do serviço secreto alemão August Hanning foi detido nesta terça-feira sob suspeita de tentativa de traição, em um caso que figura entre os maiores escândalos de inteligência da Alemanha desde a Guerra Fria. O Ministério Público o acusou de pagar por documentos secretos e de utilizá-los em uma análise para um serviço de espionagem estrangeiro. Não foi identificado o serviço de inteligência em questão, e não ficou claro imediatamente se a análise chegou ao destinatário pretendido. A prisão de um ex-chefe da inteligência externa da Alemanha não tem precedentes e pode prejudicar as relações de inteligência do país com nações aliadas, segundo um parlamentar sênior da área de segurança. “Hanning é fortemente suspeito de espionagem traidora, obtenção de segredos de Estado, tentativa de traição e espionagem”, afirmou o Ministério Público em comunicado. A revista “Der Spiegel” noticiou na noite desta terça-feira (horário local) que os investigadores apuram uma possível conexão com o Azerbaijão. A publicação informou que Hanning havia mantido contato com um agente daquele país. O Ministério Público Federal preferiu não comentar a reportagem. Hanning não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. A Chancelaria se recusou a comentar. Cinco anos após o término de seu mandato de sete anos como chefe do serviço de inteligência externa BND, em 2005, Hanning combinou com um ex-gerente administrativo do BND para receber informações confidenciais de inteligência em troca de pagamento, segundo os promotores. O gerente de escritório, identificado como Manfred D. em conformidade com as regras de privacidade, também foi preso nesta terça-feira, e ambos devem comparecer perante um juiz no Tribunal Federal de Justiça. Manfred D. atuou como gerente administrativo de sucessivos presidentes do BND até março de 2026, o que possivelmente lhe deu acesso a algumas das informações de inteligência mais recentes da Alemanha na época em que, segundo os promotores, os documentos estavam sendo desviados do serviço. SEM COMPROMISSO Os promotores afirmaram que D. é suspeito de ter fornecido cerca de 2.000 documentos ao longo dos anos, incluindo material confidencial destinado exclusivamente ao uso interno do BND e a reuniões de alto escalão sobre inteligência na Chancelaria. Entre eles estavam documentos relacionados ao programa nuclear iraniano e às forças armadas russas, assim como material altamente sensível classificado como secreto por agências de inteligência aliadas em outros países, informou o jornal Sueddeutsche Zeitung (SZ). Os promotores afirmaram que Hanning utilizou informações confidenciais fornecidas por D. para preparar uma análise destinada a um oficial de um serviço de inteligência estrangeiro e, durante anos, compartilhou informações políticas com um representante da agência de espionagem. O caso não envolve a Rússia, de acordo com informações obtidas pelo Sueddeutsche Zeitung. O especialista em segurança Roderich Kiesewetter disse ao jornal Handelsblatt nesta terça-feira que o caso poderia prejudicar as relações com os aliados de inteligência da Alemanha, afirmando que casos de espionagem desse tipo são “particularmente onerosos para a confiança e particularmente prejudiciais para a Alemanha”. O presidente do BND, Martin Jaeger, afirmou que a agência iniciou investigações internas abrangentes assim que surgiram as suspeitas, acrescentando: “Não pode haver concessões em matéria de segurança interna.” ESPIONAGEM A prisão de Hanning é o mais recente de uma série de escândalos de espionagem notórios na Alemanha. O chanceler da Alemanha Ocidental, Willy Brandt, foi forçado a renunciar em 1974 após ser revelado que um espião da Alemanha Oriental havia trabalhado como seu assessor próximo por quase dois anos. Em 1990, Klaus Kuron, autoridade de alto escalão da contra-espionagem da Alemanha Ocidental, foi desmascarado como espião da Stasi e posteriormente condenado por traição. Mais recentemente, o ex-chefe da inteligência interna, Hans-Georg Maassen, afirmou em 2024 que estava sendo monitorado pela agência de segurança que ele mesmo chefiou, sob suspeita de extremismo político de direita, o que ele negou.

item.title: Peso mexicano regresa a niveles por debajo de 18/dlr, bolsa acompaña recuperación
item.description: El peso mexicano avanzó el martes por tercera jornada consecutiva, impulsado por un declive global del dólar, mientras los inversionistas esperan las minutas de las reuniones más recientes de la Reserva Federal (Fed) y el Banco de México, en busca de nuevas señales sobre las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano avanzó el martes por tercera jornada consecutiva, impulsado por un [USN:L6N45S0UT TEXT:"declive global del dólar"], mientras los inversionistas esperan las minutas de las reuniones más recientes de la Reserva Federal (Fed) y el Banco de México, en busca de nuevas señales sobre las tasas de interés. Por lo pronto, [USN:L6N45S13X TEXT:"Mary Daly"], presidenta de la Fed de San Francisco, dijo que futuros incrementos dependerán de la persistencia de las presiones inflacionarias, mientras que [USN:L6N45S166 TEXT:"Jeff Schmid"], de la Fed de Kansas City, afirmó que es probable que aún se requiera subir más el costo de los créditos para reducir la inflación. * La moneda local cotizaba en 17.9651 por dólar hacia el final de los negocios, con una apreciación del 0.60%, recuperando el umbral de 18 unidades luego de varias semanas de un rápido deterioro que la llevó a tocar el jueves las [USN:L1N45N0ZE TEXT:"18.4330 unidades"], su nivel más débil desde noviembre de 2025. * La divisa ha estado bajo presión por preocupaciones de que un mayor endurecimiento monetario en Estados Unidos reduzca el diferencial frente a los rendimientos en México, restando atractivo a las operaciones de [USN:L1N45L0OH TEXT:"carry trade"], que durante años han respaldado a los activos locales. * Sin embargo, datos del mercado [USN:L6N45O0QK TEXT:"laboral estadounidense"] divulgados el viernes llevaron a los operadores a moderar sus expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Fed en su próxima decisión del 28 de octubre. Aun así, el mercado sigue anticipando un aumento en diciembre. * Las minutas de la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"], que se conocerán el miércoles, y las del [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"Banco de México"], el jueves, serán seguidas de cerca para evaluar las perspectivas monetarias. * Los mercados también están atentos a la situación en Medio Oriente y noticias sobre la revisión del acuerdo comercial de América del Norte, TMEC, y de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato en Estados Unidos, factores que podrían añadir agitación a la moneda. * "Los riesgos a corto plazo siguen siendo elevados, pero el ajuste reciente podría haber sido suficiente para permitir cierta recuperación hacia el cierre del año", dijo BBVA. "Dado que las expectativas del mercado sobre la Fed son más agresivas que nuestro escenario base, vemos margen para que tanto el peso como la volatilidad se normalicen", agregó. * La bolsa mexicana también hiló su tercera jornada de ganancias, en un mercado que comenzó a dirigir la mirada a la temporada de resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre. El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) subió un 0.52% a 65,312.46 puntos. * Destacó un alza del 7.12% a 29.93 pesos de los títulos de la aerolínea Grupo Aeroméxico (AERO.MX) , tras divulgar sus cifras de tráfico de septiembre, aunque la compañía no forma parte de la principal muestra accionaria local. * En el mercado de deuda, los rendimientos primarios de los Certificados de la Tesorería (Cetes) registraron un desempeño mixto en la subasta semanal de valores gubernamentales, en medio de la cautela por las perspectivas de tasas. * El rendimiento del Cete de referencia a 28 días fue colocado en un 6.09%, ocho puntos básicos por encima de su remate previo, mientras que el del plazo más largo, a 721 días, bajó tres puntos básicos, a un 7.98%.

item.title: Sixers lose backup C Ariel Hukporti to torn Achilles
item.description: Philadelphia 76ers center Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn right Achilles tendon in Monday night's preseason opener.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia 76ers center Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn right Achilles tendon in Monday night's preseason opener. The team announced that he will undergo surgery on Tuesday and further updates would be provided as appropriate. The injury occurred during the first quarter of the Sixers' 120-97 win against the visiting New York Knicks. Hukporti started the game against his former team and finished with one assist and one missed shot in five minutes. The 24-year-old native of Germany signed a one-year, $3.4 million contract with Philadelphia in July after winning an NBA championship with the Knicks last season. Hukporti averaged 2.1 points, 2.7 rebounds and 9.1 minutes in 79 games (six starts) with the Knicks over the past two seasons. --Field Level Media

item.title: Louis Vuitton shows slinky dresses and fluid jackets, adapts to warming world
item.description: Louis Vuitton showed fluid jackets and slinky, sheer dresses on Tuesday as womenswear creative director Nicolas Ghesquière said hotter temperatures caused by climate change were changing his approach to developing fabrics and designing clothes.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Louis Vuitton showed fluid jackets and slinky, sheer dresses on Tuesday as womenswear creative director Nicolas Ghesquière said hotter temperatures caused by climate change were changing his approach to developing fabrics and designing clothes. "The world is getting warm," Ghesquière said after the show, asked about the heatwaves that swept Europe this summer. "It definitely has a strong influence, I think we all felt we needed a different wardrobe, we needed to think differently — it's almost like you have to weigh the clothes ... and see how they can perform, to think if they can be relevant today and for the future." Light, flowing fabrics were used throughout the spring/summer 2027 collection on simple strappy dresses, loosely fastened jackets and sheer skirts in white or pastel pink and blue. A black and white check look and dresses covered in an iridescent diamond pattern provided graphic elements in otherwise pared-back, tonal outfits. Models emerged in between Louis Vuitton-branded cars on a set made to look like a highway, with a tar floor and road markings — decor Ghesquière said was inspired by learning that the stunning Louvre courtyard was for decades used as a parking lot for finance ministry officials, before the museum's famous glass pyramids were installed. Jackets featured flowing sleeves with some also extending into a long train trailing behind the model, and trousers were wide and fluid with long slits up the side to let air in. Small, simple handbags came in cream and lemon tones. Ghesquière told reporters after the show that despite the minimalist appearance, "making things extremely light is very complex and the engineering and development of fabric to fight that gravity is also very complex". Louis Vuitton, the flagship brand of luxury giant LVMH, has struggled with falling sales of its famous monogrammed handbags as fewer middle-class shoppers feel they can stretch to high-end purchases. The monogram was used lightly in the collection, featuring only on a couple of handbags and a leather bomber jacket. A crowd of screaming fans outside the show greeted the arrival of K-pop star Felix, while France's first lady Brigitte Macron was among the celebrity guests, along with actors Zendaya, Emma Stone, and Saoirse Ronan.

item.title: US Circuit Judge, 99, gets fitness dispute moved to new court
item.description: US Chief Justice John Roberts has transferred a dispute between the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and its longest-serving judge Pauline Newman to a new federal appeals court, according to an order published on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: US Chief Justice John Roberts has transferred a dispute between the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and its longest-serving judge Pauline Newman to a new federal appeals court, according to an order published on Tuesday. Roberts' decision to move the dispute to the Atlanta-based 11th Circuit gives the oldest active federal judge an opportunity to convince a new set of judges that she should be reinstated. The order said that Roberts moved the case to the 11th Circuit in August. It was made public on Tuesday at Newman's request. Newman, a revered figure in patent law, was appointed to the Federal Circuit in 1984 by Republican President Ronald Reagan. The court handles patent appeals nationwide and frequently rules in intellectual property cases involving major companies. The Washington-based Federal Circuit suspended Newman, 99, in 2023 after she allegedly refused to cooperate with an investigation into her fitness to serve. The US Supreme Court [USN:S0N41Y00E TEXT:"declined in June"] to take up a lawsuit brought by Newman over her suspension. Newman had told the justices that the Federal Circuit had violated her constitutional rights. "We are pleased the case has been transferred," her attorney, Andrew Morris, of the New Civil Liberties Alliance said on Tuesday. "Judge Newman has been requesting a transfer for more than three years." Spokespeople for the Federal Circuit and US court system declined to comment. A panel of Federal Circuit judges noted staff reports of Newman's "memory loss, confusion, paranoia and angry rants" in [USN:L1N39L168 TEXT:"documents released"] in 2023 by the court. A council of all of the court's active judges, led by Chief Judge Kimberly Moore, unanimously voted to [USN:L1N3AW11R TEXT:"suspend Newman"] later that year after finding that she refused to cooperate with an investigation into her fitness. Newman's suspension remains in place for now. The Committee on Judicial Conduct and Disability of the Judicial Conference of the United States, part of the federal judiciary's governing body, has separately [USN:L6N40C19I TEXT:"upheld"] the suspension.

item.title: US arrests person in connection to Canada school shooting, officials say
item.description: US authorities arrested a person in Washington state on Tuesday who they accuse of providing advice and offering to live stream a deadly mass shooting carried out earlier this year in Canada.
item.dc:creator: Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: US authorities arrested a person in Washington state on Tuesday who they accuse of providing advice and offering to live stream a deadly mass shooting carried out earlier this year in Canada. James Cody Bryant, 30, was detained on a charge of conspiracy to murder people in a foreign country in connection to the shooting at [USN:O8N3WG017 TEXT:"Tumbler Ridge"], according to the Department of Justice. The charge carries a penalty of up to life in prison. Bryant was in repeated contact with the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, offering technical advice, sending money, including for the shoes to be used during the attack, and agreeing to live stream the event, law enforcement officials said. "James Cody Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to, and he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer," Acting US Attorney for the Western District of Washington Neil Floyd told reporters. Court records did not immediately list an attorney for Bryant. Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in one of Canada's worst mass shootings. Van Rootselaar, 18, who had suffered a series of mental health problems, killed her mother and stepbrother at home before shooting dead a teacher and five young students at her former school in Tumbler Ridge, a settlement of around 2,400 in the Canadian Rockies, according to police. Van Rootselaar, who police said was born a male but began identifying as a woman, then died by suicide. Bryant, who officials said they understood was also born a man but identified as female, agreed to live stream a feed of the attack and broadcast it "in a way that would maximize notoriety for the shooter," Mike Herrington, FBI Seattle special agent in charge, said. The live stream on Twitch was shut down after about 20 seconds, officials said. "Without Bryant's misplaced loyalty and willingness to operate the live stream, we don't ultimately know if the shooter would have gone through with the crime," Herrington said. "We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the live stream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the live stream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media." (This story has been corrected to fix the timing of the shooting to earlier this year in paragraph 1.)

item.title: Venezuela's Cardon refinery halted after fire, sources say
item.description: Venezuela's Cardon refinery, the country's second-largest with a 310,000-barrel-per-day capacity, was halted due to a fire at one of its processing units, eight sources with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Mircely Guanipa, Deisy Buitrago
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's Cardon refinery, the country's second-largest with a 310,000-barrel-per-day capacity, was halted due to a fire at one of its processing units, eight sources with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday. Fires, power interruptions and outages are common at facilities operated by state-run oil company PDVSA, and can affect supply of essential fuels for the domestic market, like gasoline and diesel. The fire started at a gas line that connects the refinery's diesel hydrotreater, forcing the entire facility's shutdown, including boilers, two of the sources said. PDVSA did not respond to a request for comment. The blaze was extinguished less than an hour later, following some explosions and the evacuation of personnel, according to the sources and neighbors. No injured workers have been reported. Cardon is part of PDVSA's 955,000-bpd Paraguana Refining Center, the country's largest complex. Videos posted on social media showed huge columns of flames and smoke billowing from the refinery. Later, photos shared by neighbors showed firefighters in the facility and the flames extinguished. Reuters could not immediately verify the content of the videos, but other sources reported seeing flames and smoke at the refinery. Output at one of Cardon's crude distillation units and its fluid catalytic cracker [USN:L1N45H0G3 TEXT:"was halted"] last month due to insufficient feedstock.

item.title: Saudi Arabia end 22-year wait for another Gulf Cup title
item.description: Early strikes secured hosts Saudi Arabia the 27th Gulf Cup with a 2-0 win over the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday, ending a 22-year wait to lift the trophy again.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Yossry
item.content:encoded: Early strikes secured hosts Saudi Arabia the 27th Gulf Cup with a 2-0 win over the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday, ending a 22-year wait to lift the trophy again. Winger Hammam Al Hammami opened the scoring in the 11th minute with a deflected shot from the edge of the box, sparking celebrations at King Abdullah Sports City in Jeddah. Just two minutes later, Georgios Donis' side took a 2-0 lead when Feras Al Brikan struck from close range. They almost scored again when Saleh Abu Alshamat, who started alongside his brother Mohammed, hit the bar. "We are very happy... there were many difficulties, but the players showed concentration and discipline and gave their maximum on the pitch," Donis told a press conference. "I think we turned those difficulties into a title, and that is important. We were the best team in this competition. This title gives us confidence for the future, and we have to keep showing the same qualities" he added. "BIGGER CHALLENGE AHEAD" The UAE pressed to try to close the deficit. They were awarded a penalty in the 38th minute only to see the VAR overturn the decision. After the interval, Saudi goalkeeper Mohamed Al Owais denied Sultan Adil from close range and Fabio Lima struck the bar in the 88th minute, leaving Saudi Arabia with a clean sheet throughout the tournament. The triumph followed an early and disappointing exit from this year's World Cup and gave the Saudis a fourth Gulf Cup title, their first since 2004. "After the World Cup, we knew that we had made mistakes and had some bad moments, but we learned from this experience... we improved and developed our football. And I think they deserve this result. Now, the result reflects the work" said Donis. Saudi Arabia will take on Kuwait, Oman and Palestine at the 2027 Asian Cup on home soil, with the tournament scheduled for January 7-February 5. "We have an even bigger challenge ahead, which is the Asian Cup. God willing, this (title) will give us even greater motivation to do what satisfies the national team and Saudi as a whole," Player of the Tournament Al Hammami told Alkass Sports TV.

item.title: S&P 500 e Nasdaq registram recordes de fechamento, com foco voltado para balanços
item.description: As ações nos EUA fecharam em alta nesta terça-feira, à medida que os preços do petróleo se estabilizaram e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA recuaram, oferecendo algum alívio em relação às preocupações que têm ocupado os investidores nas últimas semanas e permitindo que os mercados voltassem sua atenção para a temporada de divulgação de resultados do terceiro trimestre, que se aproxima.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: As ações nos EUA fecharam em alta nesta terça-feira, à medida que os preços do petróleo se estabilizaram e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA recuaram, oferecendo algum alívio em relação às preocupações que têm ocupado os investidores nas últimas semanas e permitindo que os mercados voltassem sua atenção para a temporada de divulgação de resultados do terceiro trimestre, que se aproxima. A alta generalizada levou o S&P 500 e o Nasdaq a recordes de fechamento. O índice Dow Jones, composto por ações de grande capitalização, permanece a pouco mais de 5% de seu nível recorde de fechamento alcançado em 5 de agosto. Quando os preços do petróleo se estabilizam ou caem, “isso faz com que os rendimentos caiam, pois há menos ansiedade em relação à inflação impulsionada pela energia, o que, por sua vez, está ajudando a elevar as ações”, disse Oliver Pursche, vice-presidente sênior da Wealthspire Advisors, em Nova York. “Essa tem sido a narrativa do mercado nas últimas duas semanas.” O setor de IA continua em alta, com o Índice de chips Philadelphia SE Semiconductor (.SOX) ganhando terreno. Os gastos com infraestrutura relacionada à IA se refletiram nos dados do comércio internacional, que mostraram que as importações de bens de capital aumentaram 4,4% em agosto. O relatório do Departamento de Comércio mostrou que o déficit comercial dos EUA cresceu 13,7%, à medida que as importações atingiram novo recorde. Em termos mensais e anuais, as importações cresceram 4,3% e 28,4%, respectivamente, refletindo uma demanda interna robusta que poderia agravar as pressões inflacionárias, especialmente em meio a restrições de oferta relacionadas à guerra. Mesmo assim, os mercados financeiros estão atualmente precificando uma probabilidade decrescente de 19,4% de que o Federal Reserve dos EUA implemente seu segundo aumento consecutivo das taxas de juros na reunião de política monetária deste mês, abaixo dos 50,9% registrados há uma semana, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. As apostas no aumento da taxa pelo Fed têm reagido aos preços do petróleo, que dispararam em meio à guerra no Irã, ameaçando se transformar em pressões mais amplas sobre os preços. Mas as preocupações com a oferta diminuíram depois que os países do G7 chegaram a um acordo para liberar estoques de emergência de diesel e petróleo bruto, ajudando a estabilizar os contratos futuros de petróleo WTI e Brent com vencimento no mês seguinte. “Não esperamos que (o Fed) tome nenhuma medida na próxima reunião”, disse Tim Ghriskey, estrategista sênior de portfólio da Ingalls & Snyder, em Nova York. “Mas acho que eles estão em um ciclo de aumentos graduais.” “Os altos preços do petróleo afetaram uma ampla gama de consumidores”, acrescentou Ghriskey. “Essa é uma das razões para o recente aumento das taxas pelo Fed.” O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 0,49%, para 51.521,04 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) ganhou 0,58%, para 7.818,95 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) avançou 0,45%, para 27.599,79 pontos. Dos 11 principais setores do S&P 500, todos, exceto o de saúde (.SPXHC) , registraram alta, com o setor de serviços públicos (.SPLCRU) liderando o movimento. A temporada de divulgação dos resultados do terceiro trimestre começa na próxima semana, com várias empresas financeiras de grande destaque previstas para divulgar seus resultados na próxima terça-feira. Atualmente, os analistas esperam um crescimento anual dos lucros do S&P 500 de 30,6%, no total, para o período de julho a setembro, liderado por um salto esperado de 114,7% nos lucros do setor de energia, seguido por um aumento estimado de 66,5% nos resultados do setor de tecnologia, de acordo com a LSEG. A Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) subiu 5,8% após o aumento da previsão de receita para 2028 da fabricante de chips, devido à forte demanda por seus chips para data centers. A fabricante de chips AMD (AMD.O) registrou alta de 2,8% depois que a presidente-executiva Lisa Su afirmou que a empresa planeja aumentar substancialmente o fornecimento de chips em 2027 para atender à crescente demanda por IA. A Constellation Energy (CEG.O) saltou 12,3% após a Alphabet (GOOGL.O) firmar um contrato de fornecimento de energia de 3.590 megawatts com a empresa. A Option Care Health (OPCH.O) disparou 32,7% depois que a distribuidora de medicamentos McKesson (MCK.N) e a empresa de private equity Clayton Dubilier & Rice concordaram em comprar a provedora de terapia de infusão em um negócio avaliado em cerca de US$5,8 bilhões, incluindo dívidas.

item.title: Refinería venezolana de Cardón se detuvo tras un incendio, según dos fuentes
item.description: La refinería Cardón de Venezuela, la segunda más grande del país con una capacidad de 310.000 barriles por día, fue paralizada debido a un incendio en una de sus unidades de procesamiento, dijeron el martes ocho fuentes con conocimiento del asunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La refinería Cardón de Venezuela, la segunda más grande del país con una capacidad de 310.000 barriles por día, fue paralizada debido a un incendio en una de sus unidades de procesamiento, dijeron el martes ocho fuentes con conocimiento del asunto. Incendios, fallas operativas y cortes de energía son comunes en las instalaciones operadas por la petrolera estatal PDVSA, lo que puede afectar el suministro de combustibles esenciales para el mercado interno, como gasolina y diésel. El incendio comenzó en una línea de gas que conecta el hidrotratador de diésel de la refinería, lo que obligó a paralizar toda la instalación, incluidas las calderas, dijeron dos de las fuentes. La petrolera estatal PDVSA no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. El incendio fue extinguido menos de una hora después, tras algunas explosiones y la evacuación del personal, según fuentes y vecinos. No se han reportado trabajadores heridos. Cardón es parte del Centro de Refinación Paraguaná de 955.000 bpd de PDVSA, el complejo más grande del país. Los vídeos publicados en las redes sociales mostraban enormes columnas de llamas y humo saliendo de la refinería. Posteriormente, fotografías compartidas por vecinos mostraban a los bomberos en las instalaciones y el fuego extinguido. Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato el contenido de los vídeos, pero otras fuentes informaron haber visto llamas y humo en la refinería. La producción en una de las unidades de destilación de crudo de Cardón y su craqueador catalítico fluidizado se detuvo el mes pasado debido a la insuficiencia de materia prima.

item.title: NYC sues Manhattan law firm alleging bogus injury suits
item.description: The city of New York has sued a small Manhattan law firm for allegedly bringing bogus slip-and-fall lawsuits against it in violation of federal anti-racketeering law.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: The city of New York has sued a small Manhattan law firm for allegedly bringing bogus slip-and-fall lawsuits against it in violation of federal anti-racketeering law. The city, in a complaint filed Sunday in Manhattan federal court, cited 15 allegedly fraudulent lawsuits brought by Asher & Associates and its attorneys, Ryan and Roberta Asher. The Asher firm claimed its clients were injured riding motorcycles, scooters and bicycles on poorly-maintained city roads when they were actually injured in other ways, like a fight or a hit-and-run incident, the city said. The Asher firm dropped its cases without explanation after the city confronted it with "contradictory statements" in the lawsuits, New York's Law Department said in a press release. “Personal injury laws exist to protect actual victims of trauma, not to line the pockets of people looking to make a quick buck off City taxpayers,” New York City Corporation Counsel Steven Banks said in a statement. Ryan and Roberta Asher did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The case is the latest around the country to target personal injury lawyers under the federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, a 56-year-old law passed by Congress to help rein in organized crime bosses who were often insulated by foot soldiers, for a pattern of unlawful behavior. Damages are tripled under RICO if the plaintiff wins. New York is also seeking damages under the city and state False Claims Act. “Fraudulent personal injury lawsuits profit on the misfortune of others and taxpayers bear the burden,” New York City Department of Transportation Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. The city in its lawsuit said the 15 cases it cited are "the tip of the proverbial iceberg," and that it seeks to discover other lawsuits by the Asher firm that have allegedly generated "millions of dollars in legal fees, settlements and judgments based on false narratives." Companies including Uber Technologies and Federal Express Corporation [USN:L6N41R1BP TEXT:"have filed a string of lawsuits"] invoking civil RICO provisions against plaintiffs' lawyers in US federal courts. Nearly 300 such cases have been filed since 2024, according to a report released Tuesday by the American Tort Reform Association, a pro-business legal advocacy group. The case is The City of New York v. Ryan H Asher, et al., US District Court for the Southern District of New York, 1:26-cv-08753 For the city: Eric Proshansky and Cesar Ruiz of the New York City Law Department

item.title: Russia says tanker crew rescued in Black Sea after attack set ship ablaze
item.description: Emergency crews on Tuesday rescued the 23-member crew of a Liberian-flagged tanker, the Aframax Rio, which was set ablaze off Russia's Black Sea coast after coming under attack from an unmanned vessel, the Russian Transport Ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emergency crews on Tuesday rescued the 23-member crew of a Liberian-flagged tanker, the Aframax Rio, which was set ablaze off Russia's Black Sea coast after coming under attack from an unmanned vessel, the Russian Transport Ministry said. The ministry, in a report posted on Telegram, said the crew was made up entirely of Indian nationals. It said there were no injuries. The ministry said firefighters had sufficient means to tackle the blaze once it became less intense. Russian regional authorities in the settlement of Sirius had earlier reported the fire aboard the tanker. Beaches in the settlement in Russia's south Krasnodar region were closed to the public, the authorities said.

item.title: Trump says he is thinking about suspending federal gas tax
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was thinking about suspending the federal gas tax as high gas and diesel prices pose a risk to his Republican Party heading into the November midterm US elections.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was thinking about suspending the federal gas tax as high gas and diesel prices pose a risk to his Republican Party heading into the November midterm US elections . DETAILS AND QUOTES: "We're thinking about that," Trump said when asked if the federal gas tax should be suspended, without providing more details. Trump has also [USN:S0N41B038 TEXT:"previously expressed support"] for suspending the US gas tax in recent months. Trump's comments came a day after he [USN:L1N45R0NK TEXT:"signed an executive order"] to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that he unveiled from a rally stage in Nebraska. High gas and diesel prices are a risk to Trump ahead of the midterm elections in which control of Congress is at stake. Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the Senate and House of Representatives. Waiving the 18.4-cent federal gasoline tax requires Congress to pass legislation. Fuel prices have risen in response to the US-Israeli war on Iran and the Russian invasion of Ukraine , with the conflicts having led to attacks on refineries in the Middle East and Russia. Trump's approval rating has held at [USN:L6N45R122 TEXT:"a record low"] 32% in recent days, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday, with Americans most concerned about the high cost of living, spurred by soaring gasoline and diesel prices.

item.title: Anthropic opens its most powerful AI models to more security teams
item.description: Anthropic is expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its most powerful AI models with fewer safeguards, after its Project Glasswing initiative helped uncover more than 100,000 software vulnerabilities this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic is expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its most powerful AI models with fewer safeguards, after its Project Glasswing initiative helped uncover more than 100,000 software vulnerabilities this year. Its partners under Glasswing, an initiative aimed at securing the world's most critical software, found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July. Anthropic's own open-source scanning found 5,500 more between April and October. More than 33,000 have so far been rated critical or high severity. Anthropic said the figures are likely an undercount and expects the true impact to be at least five times higher, as the data comes from a survey of a limited number of partners. The revamped Cyber Verification Program, or CVP, announced on Tuesday combines two programs Anthropic has run for the past six months. The first, Glasswing, gave organizations securing critical software access to Claude Mythos, Anthropic's most cyber-capable family of models. The second, the original CVP, gave vetted security teams reduced safeguards on Claude Opus and Sonnet models. The company's April unveiling of Claude Mythos Preview raised fears that AI could hack software before it had been secured. The new program has three tiers, each with its own verification requirements and security controls. All three include access to Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Mythos 5.1 and future models. The Defense tier covers work such as incident response and malware analysis. Security teams, critical infrastructure operators, open-source maintainers and researchers with a record of reported vulnerabilities can apply. The Red Team tier adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming, but only organizations can apply. The Specialized tier has the fewest restrictions and is reserved for a small group of organizations authorized to test safety-critical systems such as power grids, flight systems and interbank transfer infrastructure. Anthropic vets each member together with the US government, and existing Glasswing members will move into this tier.

item.title: 'I'm getting fed up': early US midterm voters line up before dawn in Ohio
item.description: Voters started lining up while it was still dark on Tuesday morning at the Medina County Board of Elections as early voting began in Ohio, a state that looms large in the nationwide campaigns between Republicans and Democrats battling for control of the US Congress.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan
item.content:encoded: Voters started lining up while it was still dark on Tuesday morning at the Medina County Board of Elections as early voting began in Ohio, a state that looms large in the nationwide campaigns between Republicans and Democrats battling for control of the US Congress. By the time polling in the northeast Ohio county closed for the day, Democrats' turnout eclipsed that of Republicans' in a possible early sign that they are more motivated to vote this year. Though turnout is typically higher in presidential elections, which are run every four years, this year's midterm voters in Ohio have a say in one key US Senate race and two for the US House of Representatives that are seen as "toss-ups," according to the Cook Political Report. Registered Republicans, Democrats and independents interviewed by Reuters all shared similar frustrations: they are exhausted by political ads they see as deceptive and mean, they hate the US war with Iran and they really hate the inflation that they believe has become chronic. Nobody said they expected things to improved any time soon. The third person in line waiting for polling to open at 8 a.m. (1200 GMT) was Eddie St. John, 83, a retiree from the town of Wadsworth. Asked what he most wanted to see fixed as a result of the election, which ends on November 3, St. John said, "Mostly it's our economy. It sucks." "You can't afford nothing anymore. Everything's so high. Gas is getting worse all the time," he said, adding, "This guy in office now he promises this. He promises that... (but) nothing's coming down." "This guy," St. John said, is President Donald Trump, who isn't on the ballot but whom the voter said he blames more than political parties. INFLATION, WAR ON BALLOT The party in power usually suffers in midterm elections. With Republicans holding the White House and both chambers of [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"Congress at a time when Trump's approval rating"] is at a record-low 32%, Democrats are feeling increasingly competitive. Political analysts will be watching closely what unfolds in Ohio, as Trump has been a dominant force, especially among blue-collar workers who used to align with the Democratic Party. But with inflation running at around 3.4%, there is deep discontent over rising food, energy and housing costs. The US war with Iran, launched by Trump on February 28 for reasons that critics say he has not clearly articulated, also has voters worried that it will become yet another "forever war." Troy Flohr, 59, a retired policeman with the Medina County Sheriff, complained about the array of campaign ads that he said were riddled with "half-truths." Standing just feet away from a voting booth, Flohr said he usually backs Republicans but was still undecided whether to vote to reelect Republican Representative Max Miller for a third term. "I tend to like the rest of them" running as Republicans on this year's ballot, Flohr added. He said his nephew is serving in the US Army and stationed in the Middle East. Without mentioning Trump by name, he said, "I'm tired of him saying the war's going to end in two weeks, the war's going to end next month...I'm getting fed up with that." Yet Flohr said he would "probably" vote for Trump again given the chance. "I don't like where the Democrat Party has gone. I'm going to leave the rest of that comment alone," he said when asked to elaborate. INDEPENDENTS Trump won Ohio and the state's 17 electoral votes handily in 2016, 2020 and 2024, despite losing the 2020 presidential race to Democrat Joe Biden. This election could depend on whether disaffected Democrats return to their party and whether many independents turn their backs on Trump's Republicans. Medina County, seen as a swing district, has 132,345 registered voters of which 29,466 are Republicans and 15,872 Democrats. Election officials say there are 86,762 independents, who could determine whether Republicans continue their success there. Despite Republicans' advantage in registered voters in the county, 499 Democrats cast ballots on Tuesday, compared to 374 Republicans, along with 291 independents. That is a significant reversal from the first day of voting in 2024, when 369 Democrats voted, compared to 702 Republicans and 433 independents, according to county data. Even more telling is data from the 2022 midterm election, when 198 Republicans cast a vote in the first day of early voting, compared to 139 Democrats and 68 independents. SENATE SEAT IN PLAY Former Senator Sherrod Brown, a Democrat from Ohio, is trying to return to the Senate, where he served for 18 years before being defeated two years ago by Republican Senator Bernie Moreno. This time around, Brown, a populist Democrat who long railed against US trade deals with foreign competitors, is attempting to unseat Republican Jon Husted in a special election with the winner holding the seat through 2028. Political analysts see the race between Husted and Brown as a toss-up. With Republicans currently holding a 53-47 majority in the Senate, Democrats are hoping for a net gain of at least four seats, including in Ohio, in order to control the chamber. CLOSE HOUSE RACES Meanwhile, two neck-and-neck US House races could help determine next year's majority in that chamber, which Republicans currently hold with a 218-214 margin. One independent is aligned with Republicans and there are two vacancies that will be filled in the midterm elections. In the 7th congressional district, which includes Medina, just south of Cleveland, incumbent Miller is seen facing a tough challenge from Democrat Brian Poindexter. While Miller has raised far more funds than his Democratic opponent and has Trump's endorsement in a Republican-leaning district, his campaign has been hit by allegations of domestic violence, which he denies. Poindexter is a labor union ironworker and member of a suburban city council. Meanwhile, in Ohio's 9th congressional district that covers most of northwest Ohio and hugs the shores of Lake Erie, Democratic Representative Marcy Kaptur, a moderate who was first elected in 1982, is battling in another toss-up race against Republican challenger Derek Merrin, who nearly defeated her in 2024. Annie Wild, 64, a retired public school teacher, said she will vote for all Democrats on the ballot. She also said since the early days of Trump's second term she has begun to see some of the president's supporters saying they are abandoning him. But that is not coming from the voters she called "MAGA." "I've lost friends that I've had for 50 years," she said of some Trump supporters, because of the gulf between them.

item.title: Bellingham hails Kane as England's greatest after milestone appearance
item.description: Jude Bellingham hailed teammate Harry Kane as England's greatest-ever player after the captain marked his record-equalling 125th appearance by scoring two goals and creating another in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jude Bellingham hailed teammate Harry Kane as England's greatest-ever player after the captain marked his record-equalling 125th appearance by scoring two goals and creating another in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic. Kane drew level with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most-capped men's player and celebrated the milestone by taking his tally to 91 international goals in front of an appreciative home crowd at Wembley. "First and foremost he is an unbelievable human being, as a captain and a man," Bellingham told ITV. "He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him. He is pretty unmatched. He is scoring goals for fun, he goes deep and he gets tackles in. He is only getting better." Kane helped create England's opener with a cross that was turned into his own net by Czech defender Vladimir Coufal before adding two goals of his own, prompting manager Thomas Tuchel to pay tribute to his striker's consistency. "It's what he does," Tuchel said. "I don't take it for granted, it's just exceptional every single match." Kane's latest milestone came at the stadium where his England journey began more than 11 years ago. The Bayern Munich striker made an instant impact on his 2015 debut when he came off the bench against Lithuania in a European Championship qualifier and scored 79 seconds later. "It's always special, even just walking out now and seeing the stadium, just the excitement of what's to come," Kane said before kickoff. "I try and never take it for granted. It's obviously a special night tonight, but as always, we've got to focus on the job." Kane, who also rattled a shot off the crossbar on Tuesday, has become one of the defining figures of the national team, breaking Wayne Rooney's scoring record and surpassing him as England's most-capped outfield player at the World Cup earlier this year. KANE CLOSES IN ON CENTURY The 33-year-old also broke Gary Lineker's England men's World Cup scoring record this past summer, drawing level on 10 with a double against Croatia, then moving clear with a goal against Panama. By the end of the tournament, Kane had extended the record to 14 World Cup goals. He also holds the England record for major tournament appearances with 36, goals at major tournaments (21), major tournament games as captain (32) and goals at Wembley (31). And now, he is nine shy of the elusive 100-goal mark that only three male players have reached in history in Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo, Argentina great Lionel Messi and Ali Daei of Iran. "He's at the level where tonight, this is what we expect of him: two, three goals, whatever. The guy's a machine," former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said on ITV's broadcast. "That desire to score goals, it's fantastic." "The hardest people to impress sometimes are your teammates and they all speak so highly of him, talk about how brilliant he is on the pitch, he's also got a good attitude ... he deserves everything that comes his way." Shilton, whose cap record has stood since 1990, posted a congratulatory message on X. "You will go on and beat (the record) in November, I'm sure of that, and maybe go on and set a record that will never be beaten," he said in a video. "Because you're still going strong, Harry, still playing well and scoring goals, and I know how much dedication and hard work you've actually put into achieving this."

item.title: Yemeni government fighters shown driving vehicles over Houthi opponents
item.description: Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war.
item.dc:creator: Edward Carron
item.content:encoded: Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war. The videos gave a glimpse into the brutal closing stages of a pitched battle for control of territory near the strait that the Houthis had captured last month. The Houthi advance sent shockwaves through the oil market and pushed up petrol and diesel prices worldwide. Fighting continued near Bab el-Mandeb on Tuesday as Saudi-backed government forces battled to consolidate [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"Monday's counter-attack"], besieging Houthi fighters at a military camp near the strait and pushing into hills to the east, Yemeni military sources said. The videos, verified by Reuters and filmed from inside the armoured vehicles, showed them striking fighters with their vehicles. Some were armed and some were walking or running. However, others were unarmed and some were sitting, lying or crouching on the sandy shore and made no move to evade the oncoming vehicle as they were run over. At one point, a vehicle hits a man, running and unarmed, and another crouching on the ground. It then loops back to drive over two men, both with their hands up and unarmed. Shooting can be heard during the video and at one point the vehicle's windscreen is cracked by a gunshot. A Houthi statement decried the videos as proof of war crimes, saying they showed "the true nature of the Saudi regime and the forces it has mobilised from extremist factions". Asil al-Saqladi, spokesperson for the Giants Brigade — the main Yemeni government force involved in the fighting at Bab el-Mandeb this week — said the force was conducting an investigation into the incident. He added that the brigade had been misled into believing that the Houthi fighters there were surrendering but that some of them had then fired on the government force. The Saudi-led coalition backing the government forces in Yemen did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the videos or the Houthi accusations of war crimes. The Homeland Shield Forces, a significant formation in the Yemeni government's military coalition, did not comment directly on the videos but issued a directive on Tuesday urging troops to treat prisoners well and adhere to religious, ethical and legal standards. Rights groups have previously accused the Houthis of war crimes, including sniper and shelling attacks on civilian targets, seizures of aid, abuse of prisoners and use of child soldiers. The group has denied war crimes. 'TURNING POINT' Reuters has not been able to independently verify the extent of government gains and the Houthis denied they had lost ground, saying the government claims of advances were baseless. Intense fighting meanwhile continued around Yemen's third-largest city of Taiz, where Houthi gains in a mountain district have in recent days cut off a main road to Aden, leaving government forces encircled. Yemen's [USN:L6N3Y307N TEXT:"civil war"] pits the Houthis against an uneasy coalition of sometimes rival military forces under the internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia and its allies. The renewed clashes have added a new front to the Iran-US conflict , with the [USN:L6N45308G TEXT:"US rebuffing"] Saudi requests for military help to reverse Houthi gains on the Red Sea coast near Bab el-Mandeb last month and end the group's missile and drone attacks on their territory. "The operation itself is significant because it's a turning point in the trajectory of the conflict between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition," said Ahmed Nagi, Yemen analyst at International Crisis Group. "The biggest test will be when they move towards the mountains," he added. RELIGIOUS AND REGIONAL FAULTLINES The Giants Brigade is a southern military formation originally formed by students at ultra-conservative Sunni Muslim religious colleges. That background gives both a religious and regional edge to their enmity with the Houthis, who originate in north Yemen and belong to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam. The Giants have themselves fractured this year, splitting between factions backed by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, illustrating the internal divisions that have long beset the Yemeni government's efforts to fight the Houthis. As well as further squeezing global trade routes after Iran's disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the conflagration in Yemen has brought the conflict more directly to Saudi Arabia, a US ally. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports, oil refineries and pipelines. Residents of the Saudi capital Riyadh reported hearing booms overnight and two of the kingdom's [USN:L1N45S0BG TEXT:"southern airports"] were targeted. Saudi Arabia's intervention in the latest wave of fighting included intense air strikes on Houthi forces on Monday as the Giants Brigade advanced along the flat coastal strip towards Bab el-Mandeb.

item.title: Cardinals LT Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps) out for season
item.description: Arizona Cardinals placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve for the third straight year and he will miss the remainder of the season with a torn left biceps, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arizona Cardinals placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve for the third straight year and he will miss the remainder of the season with a torn left biceps, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Tuesday. Johnson sustained the injury in the fourth quarter of Arizona's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday. "I don't know exactly when (surgery is) going to happen, but it's going to happen soon to get the process going. I know I was quick on that," LaFleur said. "I feel for him -- just all these guys. It sucks for him, first and foremost. It sucks obviously for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But it's NFL football -- here we are in October and the show goes on." Rookie Jayden Williams, who was a seventh-round pick out of Mississippi, replaced Johnson on Sunday. Arizona also placed tight end Hunter Long (right knee) on injured reserve, signed tight end Tegan Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster and signed offensive tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. from the Buffalo Bills' practice squad to the team's active roster. In other moves, tight end Kenny Yeboah, offensive lineman Austin Deculus and safety Mark Perry were signed to the practice squad and offensive lineman Vershon Lee and cornerback D'Shawn Jamison were released from the practice squad. Johnson, 25, started all four of his games this season and all 47 in which he has played since being selected by the Cardinals with the sixth overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Ohio State. Wills, 27, played in 58 regular-season games (57 starts) and two playoff games (both starts) for the Cleveland Browns from 2020-24. He injured his knee in a 2023 game against the Cardinals, played in just five games in 2024 and missed the entire 2025 season. Wills signed with the Chicago Bears in March and, after dealing with a back issue, was released on Aug. 30. He signed with the Bills on Sept. 1. Cleveland selected Wills with the 10th overall pick of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Alabama. Long, 28, has two receptions on two targets for 15 yards in four games as a reserve this season. He has played on 33% of the offensive snaps (91) and 53% of special teams snaps (57). He has 22 career receptions for 168 yards and two touchdowns in 50 games (eight starts) for the Miami Dolphins (2021-22), Los Angeles Rams (2023-24), Jacksonville Jaguars (2025) and Cardinals. Arizona obtained him and a 2028 seventh-round pick in an Aug. 30 trade with the Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round selection. Miami picked Long in the third round of the 2021 draft out of Boston College. The Cardinals (1-3) host the Lions (2-2) on Sunday in Glendale, Ariz. --Field Level Media

item.title: Thousands of European wind and solar power systems exposed online, Dutch researchers say
item.description: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie van den Berg, Toby Sterling
item.content:encoded: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday. The exposed systems included administrative and login interfaces as well as operational interfaces showing data and controls. However, one of the researchers, Soufian El Yadmani, from internet-scanning company Modat, told Reuters that researchers believed full control would have been possible in the case of around 181 sites. One turbine's web page showed live data, "Start, Stop and Reset" buttons and the turbine's location, the research said. Some systems controlled several turbines or a whole farm. "What we can map in hours, an attacker can map in hours too," the report said. The researchers urged operators to take admin interfaces off the internet immediately. SPANISH SOLAR, GERMAN WIND MOST EXPOSED The findings come amid [USN:L8N45F1L2 TEXT:"concerns about Europe's critical infrastructure,"] which has faced suspected sabotage and cyberattacks frequently attributed by Western governments to Russia since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russia denies any involvement. Last month, Dutch intelligence agencies, police and prosecutors warned that artificial intelligence was accelerating the threat. El Yadmani and Bouke van Laethem of the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre presented their findings on Tuesday at the ONE Conference in The Hague. Turbines or arrays closely linked to public infrastructure were a special concern, El Yadmani said. "If you can turn off the energy within the city or the airport, imagine that at a larger scale." Using machine learning to sort and cluster data, the pair said they identified 8,547 internet-facing systems they could link to at specific solar parks (7,942) and wind farms (605) in 35 European countries, which should not have been exposed to the internet. Most of the systems found were admin pages with login screens. Spain had the most exposed solar systems, with 2,766, followed by Greece with 1,860, they said. Germany has Europe's most installed solar capacity, and 672 exposed solar systems. However it had the most exposed wind systems with 212, with Italy close behind at 192. The researchers said the rankings partly reflected where they had been able to link systems to specific sites. The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity could not immediately comment. Authorities in Germany, Italy and Spain did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The report listed among its sources the Polish cybersecurity team CERT Polska's analysis of a [USN:L6N3YV10T TEXT:"December 2025 attack"] on 30 wind and solar sites in Poland, an example of the potential threat.

item.title: IMF says hedge funds' market footprint growing, merits closer scrutiny
item.description: Hedge funds have more than tripled in size in the last decade and now play increasingly critical market roles, the International Monetary Fund said Tuesday, while warning that the funds' use of leverage and overall opacity can inject risks into the financial system.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder
item.content:encoded: Hedge funds have more than tripled in size in the last decade and now play increasingly critical market roles, the International Monetary Fund said Tuesday, while warning that the funds' use of leverage and overall opacity can inject risks into the financial system. The findings were published Tuesday by the IMF as it released a chapter of its Global Financial Stability Report, which will be released in full on Oct. 13. Here's what the group found: Hedge funds are playing an increasingly prominent role in trading, liquidity and risk transfers, as assets at the funds now stand at roughly $13 trillion in early 2026, up significantly from just $4 trillion in 2013 Hedge fund growth has primarily come through leverage, including synthetic leverage through derivatives Such funds have grown their footprint significantly in sovereign bond markets, particularly US Treasuries. Hedge funds now account for 9% of the Treasury market, compared to just 4% in 2022 While greater hedge fund presence can boost market efficiency, the IMF warned they can also amplify stress when markets deteriorate, particularly due to those firms' use of leverage and fewer constraints on risk The IMF warned that hedge funds remain "inherently opaque," making it difficult to accurately gauge their risks and exposures. It called on policymakers to close data gaps and boost risk monitoring of the sector for potential vulnerabilities

item.title: Marvell raises 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data center demand
item.description: Marvell Technology raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, above Wall Street estimates, as demand for its custom data center chips grows along with a surge in AI spending.
item.dc:creator: Prathik Jayaprakash, Anhata Rooprai, Max Cherney
item.content:encoded: Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, above Wall Street estimates, as demand for its custom data center chips grows along with a surge in AI spending. Shares of the Santa Clara, California-based company rose about 6%, while those of rival Broadcom (AVGO.O) advanced about 4%. "It took a long time to get this company on this path and to be a technology leader," Chris Koopmans, Marvell's president and chief operating officer, said in an interview. "We have a track record of doing what we said we're going to do." Marvell outlined a strategy in 2021 centered on custom and cloud-optimized silicon — chips specifically designed for use in data centers. It has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom since then and projects it will generate $12 billion in custom chip revenue in fiscal 2029, up from a prior target of $10 billion. The company's custom chip business has become a major growth engine, with technology companies developing in-house AI processors to reduce reliance on Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips. Marvell's stock has more than tripled in value so far this year. Marvell disclosed a deal with Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) in August that could generate up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033, if performance milestones are achieved. That same month, it raised its full-year revenue outlook to about $18 billion from $16.5 billion. On Tuesday, Marvell forecast fiscal 2031 revenue of $70 billion to $90 billion. At $80 billion, the midpoint of that range exceeds Wall Street estimates of $46.85 billion, according to four analysts polled by Visible Alpha. Analysts were expecting revenue of $18.2 billion for 2028, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: Mali troops re-enter strategic northern town after separatists withdraw
item.description: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists. Malian troops were "reinforcing their presence" in the town by Tuesday night, a government statement said, adding that this would allow for "the gradual return of public administration and basic social services". The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) took control of Kidal town six months ago in [USN:L6N41903L TEXT:"nationwide attacks"] that also killed Mali's defence minister. It had joined forces in those attacks with the regional al Qaeda affiliate, Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, known as JNIM, posing the biggest test yet to Mali's military leaders who seized power in coups in 2020 and 2021. The FLA's decision to leave Kidal came in response to airstrikes by Mali's military backed by Russian fighters, the FLA said in a statement. "The FLA specifies that this is a temporary operational measure, also intended to preserve its human and logistical capabilities intact. This methodical withdrawal from the area took place without any direct combat having yet pitted its forces against the enemy," the statement said. Mali has leaned on Russian security support for years, first from the Wagner mercenary group and then from the paramilitary group Africa Corps, which is made up of many former Wagner fighters. 'SYMBOLIC' BUT NOT DECISIVE VICTORY, ANALYST SAYS Earlier on Tuesday, Mali's military said it had launched large-scale air and ground operations in the region of Kidal. The goals of the operations included tracking down and neutralizing armed groups operating in the area, destroying their supply networks and restoring "lasting security" and free movement for people and goods, a Malian military statement said. Pro-government fighters, including Russian fighters, re-entered Kidal on Tuesday afternoon, a security source said. Malian forces and Wagner fighters retook Kidal from insurgents in November 2023, the most concrete gain from their partnership — only to lose it during the attacks in April. "A successful recapture... affirms the military-led government's authority and boosts the army's morale, particularly after several high-profile setbacks both in the north and the central regions in recent weeks," said Beverly Ochieng, associate director of Control Risks. "This is also an opportunity for Africa Corps to reprise its role as the Malian government's security guarantor after appearing to lose significant ground, including in Kidal, since April." But the change of control in Kidal is still largely "symbolic" and not "decisive" in Mali's campaign against insurgent groups, Ochieng added. A source close to the FLA leadership told Reuters that the aerial operations by Malian and Russian forces began three days ago. The source played down the significance of the FLA's withdrawal, saying it was a measure to protect lives and equipment. "For us, war is not a race against the clock," the source said.

item.title: New Maryland defense shipyard gets $6.6 billion commitment and Trump visit
item.description: Defense tech firm Anduril unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $3.7 billion shipyard in Maryland that is expected to generate 3,100 jobs, in a ceremony attended by President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Nathan Gomes, Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: Defense tech firm Anduril unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $3.7 billion shipyard in Maryland that is expected to generate 3,100 jobs, in a ceremony attended by President Donald Trump. Anduril, which was also awarded a $2.9 billion US Navy contract, said the new high-tech shipyard at Sparrows Point, Maryland, near the Port of Baltimore, would make components for the Navy's Virginia-class submarines. The investment and associated contract, together valued at up to $6.6 billion, come amid a broader push by the United States and its allies to expand arms production following Russia's invasion of Ukraine and conflicts in the Middle East. "Right here in Sparrows Point, you'll build the next generation of American submarines," Trump told a crowd of mostly students from the US Naval Academy, noting the facility will produce torpedo tubes and critical components for Virginia-class attack submarines. "American taxpayers will receive a 40% stake in the new shipyard," Trump added, although he did not indicate what the ownership mechanism would be. The US already owns four shipyards, including the Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Virginia and the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Maine, which are mostly focused on the repair and upkeep of existing ships, not construction of new vessels or components for new craft. RARE POLITICAL ALIGNMENT The project puts Trump in rare alignment with a frequent critic, Maryland Governor Wes Moore, a Democrat who is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate. Maryland and Baltimore County committed to match up to 13% of the total investment by Anduril, about $481 million, through funds that will need to be approved by local legislative bodies.
